 CLEMSON — Clemson starting quarterback Tait Reynolds went down early in the first quarter vs. Georgia Tech and was replaced by Trent Pearman.
 Reynolds, a freshman, slid to end a run on Clemson’s opening drive and stayed down, holding his left knee. He had to be helped off the field and was taken to the locker room.
 Pearman took over and Clemson ended the drive with a punt. According to Clemson radio announcer Don Munson, senior QB Christopher Vizzina “didn’t take a single snap” in practice this week as he deals with an ankle injury. He fractured his left elbow earlier this season.
 Reynolds remained out for the following drive. On Clemson’s third drive, QB-turned-receiver Chris Denson took the first snap before Pearman regained QB duties.
 Reynolds went down last week vs. Syracuse with a shoulder injury but later returned to the game.
 This is a developing story and will be updated.
